newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses dive then rally on US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses dive then rally on US jobs data.

text.p: European bourses were volatile after the release of strong U.S. jobs data for August, first dropping in reaction to a one-point dive in U.S. Treasury bonds, then rallying as the Treasury market recovered. The U.S. Labor Department said 250,000 non-farm jobs were created during the month, not much different from the consensus figure of 244,000 that economists had forecast on average.
The unemployment rate dropped to 5.1 percent in August, its lowest level in more than seven years, from 5.4 percent in July.
The problem for the markets seemed to lie elsewhere, in the data on earnings.

"Average hourly earnings, an indication of wage pressures, increased 0.5 percent to $11.80. So if you couple the increase in the payrolls with the increase in wages, it provides fairly strong incentives for the Federal Reserve to step in and raise interest rates," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp in New York.

"It (the payroll report) is a pretty mixed bag. The bond market was set up for a strong figure and it got it in the hourly earnings average," said David Hewitt, a bond strategist at Tokyo Mitsubishi International in London. In London, the FTSE index of leading London shares touched a 1ow of 3,856.8 after the dive in U.S. Treasuries, before settling around 3,878,8, down 0.2 percent from Thursday.
Paris also dropped at first, but then rallied above 2,000, before slipping back to 1,996.23 by 1320 GMT, a net rise of 0.1 percent.

The dollar, in contrast, showed little change from levels ruling before the figures were released. It was quoted at 109.25 yen, barely changed from the 109.10 European close on Thursday and at 1.4865 marks versus 1.4850.
The stock markets were worried that a strong employment report could prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next policy meeting on September 24.

U.S. markets were even more nervous than usual after the Labor Department reported on Thursday that new applications for unemployment benefits fell by an unexpectedly sharp 15,000 last week, ending four straight weeks of rises.
U.S. Treasury bonds fell on that report and the Dow Jones Average on Wall Street lost 49.94 points on Thursday to 5,606.96.
After a tentative start on Friday, the Dow was up 9.25 points at 5,616.21 at 1340 gmt.

The French markets were helped by news of planned income tax cuts plus higher taxes on tobacco and alcohol. The government also predicted that economic growth would rise to 2.3 percent in 1997 from a forecast 1.3 percent this year.
The franc, weak of late due to worries about industrial unrest as the government imposes a tight budget, was steadier at 3.4205 per mark.
Worries about how the Spanish government will cut its budget deficit hurt the Madrid bourse, which was down around 0.6 percent at 1315 GMT.
Trading in gold was just as confused after the data, with the price per ounce settling eventually at $385.50 after testing support at $385.
CURRENCIES AT 1320 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4865 marks and 109.25 yen, barely changed from 1.4850 and 109.10 on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1320 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 8.4 points at 3,878.8.
Frankfurt's IBIS index was up 1.07 points at 2,533.62.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 2.45 points at 1,988.68.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1320 GMT
Gold was quoted at $385.50 against $386.35 at the close on Thursday.
